project.name: Shiloh Smart Church
project.publicModelNotice: This public digital twin communicates design intent and verified equipment requirements. Exact security-device coordinates, intrusion zones, private network addressing, rack location, cable routes, credentials, serial numbers and blind-spot analysis belong in the restricted engineering layer and are intentionally not published here.

rooms.name: Sanctuary
rooms.plain: Four 4K cameras cover the large room for security without turning the worship space into a surveillance experience.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 4 × G6 Mini Dome 4K PoE. Final mounting height, lens direction, occlusion, lighting and cable path are field-survey items. Audio recording remains disabled by default.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.plain: Security coverage is designed around doors and room overview while keeping cameras away from heat, steam and grease plumes.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 2 × G6 Mini Dome 4K PoE. Environmental conditions, hood locations, mounting surface and cable pathway require field verification.

rooms.name: Mess Hall
rooms.purpose: Community meals, meetings and flexible programming.
rooms.plain: Two opposing security views are planned, with Wi-Fi coverage sized by the final RF survey rather than guesswork.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 2 × G6 Mini Dome 4K PoE. Room geometry, occupancy, AP placement and camera sight lines remain survey-dependent.

rooms.name: Office Suite
rooms.purpose: Three private mini-offices with shared circulation.
rooms.plain: The default design watches the office entrance and common circulation, not private desks or conversations.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 2 × G5 Dome Ultra 2K covering common circulation, with intrusion contacts on individual office doors. In-office cameras require an explicit policy decision.

rooms.name: Lower-Level Circulation
rooms.purpose: Hallways and approaches to lower-level rooms.
rooms.plain: Secondary cameras protect movement paths and room approaches while privacy-sensitive rooms remain excluded by policy.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 4 × G5 Dome Ultra 2K across lower-level circulation/approaches. Exact room inventory and views must be confirmed during walkthrough.

rooms.name: Vertical Circulation
rooms.plain: Security views cover inter-floor movement without obstructing egress.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 2 × G5 Dome Ultra 2K at stair/landing positions. Stair geometry and final mounting points are not yet frozen.

rooms.name: Four Controlled Entrances
rooms.purpose: Three single exterior openings plus one main double-door opening.
rooms.plain: The doors are treated as commercial construction and life-safety systems, not four consumer smart locks.
rooms.engineering: Reference architecture: four replacement openings, one 8-door access hub, three G3 Reader Flex units, one G3 Intercom, door-position sensing, request-to-exit and code-compliant electrified hardware selected only after measured opening and egress review.

rooms.name: Five-Corner Perimeter
rooms.plain: Two crossing views are planned at each of the five exterior corners so the perimeter is not dependent on one camera angle.
rooms.engineering: Reference design: 10 installed G6 Bullet 4K PoE cameras, two views per user-identified exterior corner, plus one cold spare. Public site does not publish exact aiming, blind-spot or mounting-coordinate data.
rooms.measurementStatus: Corner geometry and FOV verification pending

systems.name: Network Core
systems.plain: One managed backbone keeps public Wi-Fi, church administration, security systems and the AI lab from stepping on each other.
systems.engineering: Logical segmentation separates management, video, access/intrusion, administration, AI clients, AI/server systems, guest, IoT/building and future voice/AV. Exact private addressing and switch-port maps are restricted engineering data.

systems.name: Video Security
systems.plain: Thirty installed cameras record locally with enough NVR headroom to grow substantially without replacing the recorder.
systems.engineering: Acceptance requires measured retention under the final codec, frame-rate, RAID/protection and bitrate configuration. Audio is disabled by default. Exact FOV and device coordinates stay out of the public model.

systems.name: Access + Doors
systems.plain: Four entrance openings are rebuilt as commercial, code-aware access points with logged credentials and visitor intercom at the main entry.
systems.engineering: Electrified locking hardware is intentionally not frozen until door dimensions, handing, rating, ADA conditions and assembly-occupancy egress are reviewed by the appropriate licensed trades/AHJ.

systems.name: Intrusion + Environmental
systems.plain: Cameras do not replace an alarm. The building gets a separate professionally monitored intrusion layer that can still communicate if the main internet connection fails.
systems.engineering: The public model intentionally does not reveal zone numbering, sensor coordinates, panel location or response procedures. Fire alarm remains a separate life-safety system.

systems.name: AI + Learning Lab
systems.plain: Students use ordinary business PCs while the heavy AI work runs on two centralized high-memory systems, one NVIDIA and one AMD/x86.
systems.engineering: The two-node design teaches both NVIDIA/CUDA/Blackwell and AMD/x86 high-memory workflows. Legacy R620 servers are used selectively for Linux, virtualization, distributed systems, storage and infrastructure education rather than modern AI acceleration.

systems.name: Power + Resilience
systems.plain: Security and compute are split across separate battery-backed power domains so one failure does not take the whole technology plant down at once.
systems.engineering: Existing solar does not prove outage islanding or battery capability. Final UPS input voltage, receptacles, electrical-panel capacity, runtime and cooling are field-survey gates.
